title: Forms of democracy
competency: Explain the difference between liberal and social democracy and list their main features.

keywords.def: A democracy that limits government in the economy and relies on the free market.
A democracy in which government intervenes in economic and social affairs to achieve equality.
An economy run by market forces with little government control.

en.text: Liberal democracy keeps government out of economic affairs. Market forces lead, and the state only keeps order and sets basic rules. It stresses political liberty and legal equality, not economic equality. It is also called capitalist democracy, practised by most Western countries.

screens.title: Who sets the price?
screens.ask: Should the government decide the price of every shirt in Merkato?
opts: No, let buyers and sellers decide
screens.after: Some democracies leave prices to the market. This is a key idea of liberal democracy.

screens.title: 3.3.1 Liberal democracy
paras: Democracy has various forms. They differ in how much government takes part in the economy.
Liberal democracy discourages government intervention in economic affairs.
Market forces get the supreme place. It is based on a free market economy.

screens.title: The role of the state
paras: The state keeps order and gives a bare minimum of rules.
Its central idea is political and legal equality, not economic equality.
It is sometimes called capitalist democracy. Most Western countries practise it.
screens.note: REMEMBER: Liberal democracy encourages the private sector and the free market system.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A democracy that limits government in the economy and relies on the free market.
An economy run by market forces with little government control.

screens.text: What type of democracy is known for promoting a free-market system?
screens.why: Liberal democracy is based on a free market economy.
screens.clue: Which form keeps government out of the economy?

screens.text: In liberal democracy, the government plays a very big role in the economy.
screens.why: The role of government in the economy is very minimal.
screens.clue: Who leads the economy: the state or the market?

screens.ask: Liberal democracy is sometimes called ___ democracy.
screens.why: The book calls it capitalist democracy.
screens.clue: Think of the economic system of most Western countries.

screens.text: Liberal democracy stresses which kind of equality?
opts: Political and legal equality, not economic equality
screens.ans: Political and legal equality, not economic equality
screens.why: Its central idea is individual political liberty and legal equality. Economic equality is not its concern.
screens.clue: Which equality does it NOT focus on?

en.text: Social democracy gives priority to economic and social affairs, and the government intervenes in them. It aims at equality and social justice through reform. It helps the poor with social security, housing, free education and health care.

screens.title: Free school, free clinic
screens.ask: A government offers free schooling and health care to poor families. Which idea is this?
screens.after: This is the idea of social democracy: the government acts for equality and social justice.

screens.title: 3.3.2 Social democracy
paras: Governments that advance social democracy give more priority to economic and social affairs.
Its goal is equality and a classless society, through reform within capitalism.
It wants everyone to have the chance to use their abilities fully.

screens.title: What it provides
paras: Social democracy stands for social justice and economic empowerment for the poor.
It provides social security, housing, free education, health and medical care.
screens.note: REMEMBER: Governments that adopt social democracy usually intervene in economic and social affairs.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A democracy in which government intervenes in economic and social affairs to achieve equality.

screens.text: What do governments in a social democracy usually do?
opts: Intervene in economic and social affairs
screens.ans: Intervene in economic and social affairs
screens.why: That is the REMEMBER box for social democracy.
screens.clue: How is it different from liberal democracy?

screens.title: Which form?
items: Social security and housing for the poor
screens.why: Liberal: little government in the economy. Social: government acts for equality.
screens.clue: Does the government step in, or stay out?

screens.text: Through reform under the guise of capitalism, social democracy seeks to achieve equality and a classless society.
screens.why: That is the goal stated in 3.3.2.

screens.text: Chala says: "Social democracy wants to abolish all private business at once." What does the book say?
opts: It seeks equality through reform within capitalism
It has no goals about equality
screens.ans: It seeks equality through reform within capitalism
screens.why: Social democracy works through reform under capitalism, not by ending it at once.

test.text: Which form of democracy relies on a free market economy?
test.why: Liberal democracy is based on the free market.

test.text: Which form of democracy provides free education, housing and health care?
Liberal democracy is mainly concerned with economic equality.
test.why: It focuses on political liberty and legal equality, not economic equality.

test.ask: Governments in a social democracy usually ___ in economic and social affairs.
test.why: They intervene in economic and social affairs.

test.text: A government cuts its role in business to a minimum and lets prices follow supply and demand. Which form fits?
test.why: Minimal government and market forces describe liberal democracy.

notes.text: Start-up questions (what is liberal democracy; features of social democracy) are answered by the read blocks and checks.
Hooks about Merkato prices and free schooling are added Ethiopian examples.
